ev.q: Pooled RR estimates were independently calculated using counts of events and participants in the phase 3 trial interim analysis and phase 2b trial
In the full trial population, preeclampsia occurred among 1.8% (95% CI = 1.4%–2.3%) of vaccine recipients and in 1.4% (95% CI = 1.1%–1.9%) of placebo recipients
5.7% of infants born to RSVpreF vaccine recipients were preterm compared with 4.7% of those born to placebo recipients
more preterm births (<37 weeks’ gestation) were observed among RSVpreF vaccine recipients than placebo recipients
limiting vaccine administration to the approved dosing interval (32–36 weeks’ gestation) reduces the potential risk for preterm birth
On September 22, 2023, ACIP and CDC recommended maternal Pfizer RSVpreF vaccination in pregnant persons
A systematic literature search was completed to review evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of maternal RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy.

methods_quotes.q: Pooled RR estimates were independently calculated using counts of events and participants in the phase 3 trial interim analysis and phase 2b trial
Vaccine efficacy was calculated as (1 – [P / (1 – P)]) x 100%
All differences between vaccine group and placebo group were not statistically significant, as determined by nonoverlapping CIs.
The Work Group used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach
